summary: @servicetitan/time-zones 3.8.1 ships an obfuscated Bun-runtime dropper in preinstall
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (dictionary-indirection identifiers such as `_0xXXXX`) and, on install, checks for a local `bun` binary; if absent, it downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the archive, chmods the binary executable, and invokes it with the sibling file `math_init.js` as its argument. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated Bun bundle (rotated string array via a `WV8StW`-style shift function, numeric opcode table, scrambled-alphabet decoder) that has no relationship to the package's stated purpose of React time-zone helpers and does not appear in `dist/` or `src/` where the real library source lives. The package.json `files` manifest declares only `["dist", "src"]`, yet the published tarball ships `setup.mjs` and `math_init.js` at its root. The delivery mechanism — install-time fetch of an alternate language runtime used to execute a bundled, opaque, obfuscated payload outside Node's visibility — is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern, and combined with the undeclared-tarball-blob shape is consistent with a compromised publish for this version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
